chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Habib ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Attar, from Bashar, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The sorcerer is struck with the sword with one strike on top of his head.
ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed punishment for a sorcerer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the hadd penalty for the sorcerer (al-sahir) as execution via a single sword strike to the head, a ruling derived from Imam al-Sadiq (AS). It serves as a primary textual basis in Shia jurisprudence for the judicial punishment of sihr, distinguishing it from other capital crimes by its specific method of execution. The brevity of the chain highlights the direct transmission of this legal detail from the Imams to the early jurists.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya and Muhammad Bin Al Husayn and Habeeb Bin Al Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Hameed Al Attar, from Bashar, from Zayd Al Shahham, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The sorcerer would be struck with one strike of the sword on top of his head’.
